text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users communicate with LLMs through prompts, and prompt engineering means writing clear instructions to get better results. These models can answer questions, summarize texts and help with writing. However, they also have limits: they may give wrong information, cannot truly understand meaning, and sometimes reflect biases found in their training data.
